frontier.hypothesis: F25 — target needs arg4's LOAD emitted after the `sw 16(sp)` and arg4's ADDRESS chain emitted before it; no measured C spelling splits them, and the reason the inline form fails is that its address chain moves late too.
frontier.mechanism: calls.c:1615-1665 precomputes register args FORWARD; an inline array-element arg has its address chain emitted there and its load deferred to load_register_parameters, which runs after the stack-arg stores — that IS target's split. But our 13-attractor (arg4 fully inline) drags the whole idx[0] chain to build idx 57-61, i.e. its address chain is emitted AFTER the sw as well, which the precompute-loop reading does not predict. Something is emitting store_one_arg for the single stack argument before, not after, the register-arg precompute loop.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/calls.c around the store_one_arg call sites and the must_preallocate / args_size block (roughly lines 1277-1420 and 1667+) and establish the ACTUAL emission order of (a) the register-arg precompute loop, (b) store_one_arg for the one stack arg, (c) load_register_parameters. If store_one_arg genuinely runs first, then target's shape requires arg4's address chain to be computed OUTSIDE the call while its load stays inline — which is precisely the i2 spelling (9/91) — and the residual 9 is then two LUID tie-breaks (the reversed lbu pair, and the D_800A11D5 chain landing after the sw) rather than a structural gap. Dump sched1's output order for i2 with tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s10/idump.sh + schedscan.py and read the LUIDs the two lbu's and the D_800A11D5 chain actually get.
